points.description: The answer conveys that a queue is a data structure that stores elements in first in, first out (FIFO) order, so the first element added is the first one removed.
The answer identifies enqueue and dequeue as the main operations of a queue (adding an element at one end and removing one from the other end are equivalent wording).
points.partial_credit: Award 1 mark if only one of enqueue (add) or dequeue (remove) is identified.

rubric.notes: The central idea is that a queue is a FIFO data structure, which carries most of the marks. Full marks need the FIFO idea and both main operations, named or described in equivalent words. A student who gives only FIFO gets 3 marks, and one who names only one operation gets 1 mark from P2.
